context shim pylode_context.py: pylode is not installed in this study's venv, so both dotted imports (pylode.profiles.supermodel.model, pylode.profiles.supermodel.query.common) are rewritten in original.py and translated.ldpy to import from a single local pylode_context.py, which merges the two real source files verbatim from RDFLib/pyLODE@0d0471fb99b201182db9d3142de13fbcaee393f2. Only the unused Metadata dataclass was dropped; everything else, including fields the region never touches, is kept whole rather than trimmed field-by-field.

graph.objects(iri, SDO.image) -> for image_id in m{ {iri} sdo:image ?image_id }; each graph.value(image_id, PRED) -> m{ {image_id} pred ?v }.first() -- both trav_one_step and trav_single_value are exercised in the same region.

the region's own ImageObject(name, description, encoding_format, source, caption, url, order) call passes positional arguments in a different order than the dataclass's fields (order, url, caption), so the constructed object's .order actually holds the caption text and .caption the sh:order value. This is a real bug in the source repository, not a translation artefact: both original.py and translated.ldpy exercise the identical shim class and the identical (buggy) call, so the oracle still holds -- confirmed by driver.py's printed output showing the swapped values identically on both sides.

repair.driver: quatre appels ajoutés, un petit sujet par cas dans fixture.ttl : ex:thing-bare (image sans aucune des six propriétés : zéro solution pour chaque lecture à valeur unique), ex:thing-double (deux valeurs pour chacune des six propriétés, plus une sdo:description, seule entrée de get_descriptions), ex:thing-falsy ("", ""^^xsd:string, 0), ex:thing-unsorted (cinq images stockées à rebours de la clé de tri, qui est la légende par l'appel positionnel, et deux images identiques pour set()).
mutants_killed: .first() -> .one() sur chacune des six lectures (6 mutants)
chacune des six lectures prend la dernière valeur au lieu de la première (6 mutants)

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the loop that appends to a list, the `image_ids` variable and the seven per-property variables become one set comprehension that calls ImageObject(...) on the reads directly, in the same order of evaluation and with the same (buggy) positional order of the source; `sorted(set(images), ...)` becomes `sorted(images, ...)`. A set built element by element keeps the first of two equal images exactly as `set(list)` does.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: only the traversal becomes an island, `for image_id in m{ {iri} sdo:image ?image_id }(graph)`, one token shorter than `graph.objects(iri, SDO.image)` with its call suffix. The six `graph.value(image_id, P)` stay Python (rule 4): `m{ {image_id} p ?v }(graph).first()` is 3 tokens longer than each of them, and with only one island left a call suffix costs no more than `@graph graph`. No exception to the symmetry rule.
In the extracted header, translated.ldpy's fourteen @prefix lines weigh more than the island saves: notation > 1 on optimized.ldpy, which the header variant measures.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: the imports reduced to Graph, URIRef, DCTERMS, SDO, SH, ImageObject and get_descriptions (Dataset, Literal, eleven namespaces and eighteen shim names go); the comment on the pylode shim stays.

optimized_header.ldpy: the same Python imports (DCTERMS, SDO and SH still serve the six graph.value calls) and only `@prefix sdo:` of the fourteen; the island saves one token and the prefix line costs five, so the header variant still leaves the ldpy side slightly longer (notation 1.027).
